input.quote: If M&I and Customer are unable to agree upon the terms for renewal of this Agreement at least six (6) months prior to the expiration of the Term, then Customer may, at its option, renew this Agreement for one (1) twelve month period at the then-current terms and conditions of this Agreement. Customer shall exercise its option, if at all, by delivering written notice to M&I at least five (5) months prior to expiration of the Term.
input.rationale: There is no automatic renewal anywhere in the Agreement: § 2.1 fixes the initial term as the "Term" (eight years from the Commencement Date, p0049) "unless extended or earlier terminated", and § 2.2 is the only renewal mechanic. Renewal proper occurs only if M&I and Customer agree in writing on renewal terms, which satisfies the preferred position's primary element (mutual written agreement); the conditional automatic-renewal elements (12-month renewal cap, 30-day opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder) are therefore not engaged. The only unilateral extension right belongs to us — a Customer-only option for a single twelve-month period at then-current terms and conditions, exercisable on five months' notice — so no non-renewal notice window is imposed on Customer and no price uplift is permitted on renewal, leaving the price-increase element inapplicable. This mechanic benefits Customer and is not redlined. For the file only (not deviations): the eight-year initial term is long, and the notice choreography is front-loaded (M&I proposal 18 months out, our response within six months, option exercise five months out), which requires diligent calendaring on our side.
